headline: A US House member has proposed a draft law that would hold AI developers liable when their AI agents harm others.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: the draft is real and the text confirms its content; it is a discussion draft, not an introduced bill.
importance_line: What changed: a discussion draft would make AI developers liable for harm their agents cause to third parties, whatever care they took, unless a user changed the system on purpose or was negligent. It is a proposal, not a bill, and Darrell West of the Brookings Institution thinks action is more likely in the next Congress.
summary: CFO Dive reports that US Representative Trahan has released a discussion draft that would hold AI companies responsible when their AI agents hurt other people by doing something that would be illegal if a human did it. The draft is a proposal, not yet a bill, and Darrell West, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, says action on such a law is more likely in the next Congress.
notes: Pool item is MLex (paywalled); CFO Dive read in full. Trahan's first name is not in the text read; check before printing. Related: Sens. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) and Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) announced separate AI-agent liability legislation the week before.
